tagline: We make a number for every game. We bet the ones where the market's wrong.

games.take: Game 2 after Milwaukee's 3-2 Game 1 win. Tampa Bay turns to Drew Rasmussen (16-5, 2.67 ERA; 2-0, 1.29 ERA this postseason, 23 strikeouts in 19 innings) against rookie Logan Henderson (11-3, 2.47 ERA) for the Brewers, who are undefeated at home this postseason. The market has this nearly a coin flip and no side clears our edge bar — the -116 price is the closest to our fair number, so the lean is the home favorite. Retractable roof, no weather angle.
games.title: World Series Game 2
games.verdict: LEAN: Brewers -116 — no true edge, but the lean is Milwaukee: the price sits closest to our fair number and the Brewers already hold serve at home.

games.take: No. 6 Indiana walks into Michigan Stadium as a touchdown-plus road favorite, a number that says the market buys the Hoosiers as a genuine top-10 team rather than a paper one. The fair number backs the favorite's side of the moneyline, and the -7.5 comes at the better price (-102) than the home dog's +7.5 (-110). No true edge on the spread, but if you're picking a side, the ranked road favorite laying less than eight is the lean.
games.title: Big Ten Showdown
games.verdict: LEAN: Indiana -7.5 — no true edge, but the lean is the No. 6 road favorite at the better price.

games.matchup: Texas Tech Red Raiders @ Cincinnati Bearcats
games.take: No. 8 Texas Tech is 6-0 after a 53-25 win over Arizona State and visits Nippert Stadium for the first time, where a 4-2 Cincinnati team comes off a 45-42 loss at West Virginia. The market makes the Red Raiders a heavy road favorite, but 11.5 points is a lot to lay on the road in a conference game, and the home dog's +11.5 comes at the better price (-102 vs -110). No true edge — the lean is the home dog with the points.
games.title: Red Raiders Visit Nippert
games.verdict: LEAN: Cincinnati +11.5 — no true edge, but the lean is the home dog getting double digits at the better price.

games.take: No. 25 Oregon heads to Champaign as a 9.5-point favorite, a number that prices the Ducks as clearly the better team but still asks them to win by double digits on the road. The home dog's +9.5 comes at the better price (-102 vs -110), and that's where the lean goes in a game where the favorite has to do all the work. No true edge — just a home dog with a full touchdown-plus cushion.
games.title: Ducks at Illinois
games.verdict: LEAN: Illinois +9.5 — no true edge, but the lean is the home dog at the better price.

games.take: No. 11 Tennessee visits South Carolina as a short road underdog, and the market barely separates these two — the Gamecocks are a field-goal favorite at home with a fair number just over 50/50. The home favorite's -2.5 comes at the better price (-104 vs -108), and home field in a near-pick'em is the tiebreaker. No true edge, but the lean is the home favorite.
games.title: SEC Afternoon
games.verdict: LEAN: South Carolina -2.5 — no true edge, but the lean is the home favorite in a near-pick'em.

games.take: The primetime game: No. 7 Ole Miss at No. 19 Texas under the lights on ABC, a field-goal spread in a top-20 matchup. The fair number leans Texas, but three points is the key number and the road dog's +3 comes at the better price (-103 vs -109). No true edge — the lean is the ranked road dog getting the field goal in a game that profiles close.
games.title: Primetime in Austin
games.verdict: LEAN: Ole Miss +3 — no true edge, but the lean is the ranked road dog getting the key number.

games.take: No. 16 USC visits Wisconsin in the NBC primetime window as a field-goal favorite, and the price on the favorite is the story: USC -3 is available at even money (+100) while the home dog's +3 costs -113. When the market lets you lay the key number at even money on the better team, that's the side. No true edge on the fair number alone, but the price makes the Trojans the lean.
games.title: Trojans at Camp Randall
games.verdict: LEAN: USC -3 — no true edge, but the lean is the favorite laying the key number at even money.

games.take: The Suns' home opener against a Golden State team running on fumes: Steph Curry said he will 'probably not' play, Brandin Podziemski is out, and Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody are already out — all on the second night of a back-to-back after Friday's loss to Memphis. Phoenix is a 9.5-point favorite for good reason, and the home favorite's -9.5 comes at the better price (-101 vs -109). The lean is Phoenix, and it's the strongest lean on the card even though the board's only play in this game is the long Warriors moneyline price.
games.title: Suns Home Opener
games.verdict: LEAN: Phoenix -9.5 — the depleted Warriors are on a back-to-back without Curry, and the home favorite comes at the better price.
